subject: Polaris Labs — elastic GPU sizing and renewal options
messages:
From: Monica Santos <procurement@polaris-labs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rahul Mehta <cto@polaris-labs.com>, infra@polaris-labs.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Polaris Labs — capacity renewal: utilization-led add vs fixed tranche

Hi Ben,

We’re coming up on our Dedicated renewal window (Sep 30) and wanted to start a sizing conversation. Attached is our usage export for May (polaris_usage_May2027.csv) and an internal projection. High level:
- Current committed pool: 48 GPUs (A100-equivalent) on Dedicated.
- Avg utilization over last 90 days: 62% (token-heavy inference peaks 3x/week).
- Two recent spikes exceeded 85% sustained over 2–3 hours (we saw ~250ms p90 latency bump).

We’re evaluating two approaches before renewal:
1) Fixed tranche top-up: +24 GPUs reserved (one-time add) to avoid peaks.
2) Utilization-indexed cadence: smaller reserved add now + quarterly reprofile tied to usage triggers (e.g., sustained 75% 7-day average).

Can you help recommend which path reduces cost and risk for us? We’d like: a mutual action plan, sample SOW language for an index-based tranche, and pricing deltas (discount tiers, burst vs on-demand). Also include what telemetry we’d need to share to make quarterly reprofile decisions.

I’ve attached the CSV and a draft PO template. If useful, cc’ing Rahul for architecture constraints.

Thanks,
Monica Santos
Head of Procurement, Polaris Labs
procurement@polaris-labs.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: polaris_usage_May2027.csv, PO_template.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Santos <procurement@polaris-labs.com>
Cc: Rahul Mehta <cto@polaris-labs.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Polaris Labs — capacity renewal: utilization-led add vs fixed tranche

Monica — thanks for the data and the clear ask. Quick read-through looks good; two suggestions up front and I’ll loop in Marcus (solutions) + Kimberly (commercial) for the executive SOW.

High-level recommendation (short):
- If predictability is the priority and you can tolerate higher unit cost: fixed tranche (+24 GPUs) is simplest.
- If minimizing committed dollars while keeping availability high: go with a utilization-indexed tranche + small steady reserve now (we can automate reprofile windows).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Permission to ingest the usage CSV into our billing/observability sandbox so Marcus can run our utilization model (I’ll redact PII).
- We’ll produce two options: (A) 24-GPU reserved add + burst policy, and (B) 12-GPU reserved now + reprofile triggers + 24-GPU burst pool (example cadence: quarterly).
- Draft SOW language for option B that ties reprofile to 7‑day rolling utilization and monthly telemetry exports.

If that works, I’ll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow so Marcus can highlight what telemetry we need (per-route token histograms, prefix hit/caching, p95/p99 lags).

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 510 555 1244

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Polaris — sizing proposal prep (internal)

Team — stitching together the analysis for Polaris Labs (PL-DEAL-8742). Summary of what I pulled and recommended approach:

What we saw in their CSV (quick take):
- 90d avg GPU utilization: 62%; peak windows up to 88% (sustained multi-hour events).
- Traffic skewed: 70% of tokens come from 12% of routes (heavy long-form summarization flows).
- KV cache presence is low (~15% hit) — opportunity for caching and prefix reuse.

Proposal (technical + commercial sketch):
- Short-term: reserve 36 GPUs now (to cover steady-state + a modest buffer) + enable a 24-GPU burst pool (on-demand) for peak mitigation.
- Medium-term: quarterly reprofile window with automatic recommendation if 7-day rolling avg >75% for two consecutive windows. Reprofile actions: +6 to +12 GPUs per quarter, max scaling guardrails to limit surprise.
- Observability contract: Polaris must ship monthly telemetry exports (token histogram by route, per-model p50/p95/p99 latencies, prefix cache hit rate). We’ll provide a telemetry schema (attached SOW_draft_v2.pdf).
- Pricing: propose blended discount schedule: 10% at commit 36 GPUs, 14% at 48+, plus a lower on-demand burst rate. Also include a 60-day notice for tranche increases to manage capacity.

Risks & mitigations:
- Rapid spikes causing transient latency: mitigate with pre-warmed burst slots + routing fallback to smaller/light models for non-critical paths.
- Billing surprise for Polaris: provide a runbook and monthly cost report with token-level breakdown.

Action items before external follow-up:
- Marcus: run our utilization model against their CSV and produce a cost delta table for (36R+24B) vs (48R) vs (60R phased). Deliverable = cost/latency trade-off doc by EOD Wed.
- Kimberly: prepare SOW language for utilization-indexed tranche and update the pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_Q3.xlsx).

Attaching SOW_draft_v2.pdf and pricing_matrix_Q3.xlsx. This message is internal.

Thanks — I’ll set the walkthrough once we have the model output.

—Ben
From: Monica Santos <procurement@polaris-labs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rahul Mehta <cto@polaris-labs.com>, infra@polaris-labs.com
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Polaris Labs — capacity renewal: utilization-led add vs fixed tranche

Ben / Team — thanks for the clear options and the internal note. We prefer the utilization-indexed approach with the following constraints:
- Start with 36 GPUs reserved + a 24-GPU burst pool as you proposed.
- Quarterly reprofile is acceptable; reprofile triggers should be based on a 7-day rolling avg >75% AND approved change by one of our engineering leads.
- We’ll provide monthly telemetry exports (CSV) and a short weekly health snapshot during Q4 run-up.

Please update the SOW to include: PO number PL-2027-08-19, an implementation timeline (warm up and routing changes within 21 days of signed SOW), and an invoice cadence.

We attached PO_PL-2027-08-19.pdf (PO number provided in body) — please confirm next steps and share the final SOW + DocuSign.

Regards,
Monica Santos
Head of Procurement, Polaris Labs
procurement@polaris-labs.com
